one_line_contribution: A retrieval-time contamination-geometry study in a multi-writer agent-experience store, claiming that harm from a benign-looking wrong trajectory tracks its mere presence in the top-k (and, under natural retrieval, the logged exposure rate) rather than its share, and that a programmatic cross-writer procedure-skeleton vote whose recall grows with the number of independent writers detects it more cheaply than the reader's own LLM critique.
closest_prior_work: Two verified papers threaten the two halves. (1) A-MemGuard (arXiv:2510.02373, verified via s2cli `paper`, S2, 56 citations) is a proactive defense for LLM agent memory built on consensus-based validation across related memory entries plus a dual-memory structure — i.e. exactly D1's primitive (flag the retrieved item whose content disagrees with its peers) already applied to agent memory, not QA passages. The proposal's distinction is that its consensus is partitioned by writer identity and that recall is reported as a curve in the number of independent writers, which A-MemGuard does not do; but the proposal never cites or engages it, so the 'the population uniquely provides a vote' framing is weaker than claimed. (2) FARMA/SENTINEL (arXiv:2607.05029, verified, 2026-07-06) plants forged reasoning traces into agent memory — the closest published analogue of the 'procedure graft' and 'relabelled failure' poisons — and defends with a structural analysis detector over weighted signals, which is D1 without the writer partition. On the geometry half, the closest threats are PoisonedRAG (2402.07867, verified in the novelty card) whose ablations already sweep the number of injected texts inside a fixed top-k, and 'One Pic is All it Takes' (arXiv:2504.02132, found via s2cli), which makes the single-item-suffices claim in visual RAG. Souly et al. (2510.07192, verified) is correctly cited as the training-time count-not-fraction result; the retrieval-time analogue is a real but incremental transposition of an effect the RAG-attack literature largely assumes.
strongest_objection: The population half of the headline is manufactured by the planting design rather than discovered. All poison is concentrated in a single carrier writer at a rate of n_p = the carrier's own count of successful items of that type (~50% of that writer's same-type items), while the other writers' pools are clean by construction. A majority vote restricted to the item's own writer (D1-self) is therefore at chance by arithmetic, and any vote pool that excludes the carrier sees uncontaminated items, so 'D1 beats D1-self by >= 0.2 recall' and 'recall rises from 1 to 3 other writers' follow from where the poison was put, not from any property of populations. There is no cell in which poison is spread across two or more writers at a matched total count, i.e. no arm that can make the cross-writer vote lose; the entailment check's claim that D1-self is 'genuinely competitive' does not survive the 50% own-writer contamination rate. Secondary but concrete: P3's boundary is 0.4*h1 with h1 = harm of one forced item at k=1, and h1 is never measured or gated — the brief's own Step-0 numbers put the k=1 clean gain at only +9.1 over static3 (+21.5 over k=0) across all games, so h1 >= 24 net is doubtful; against the stated +/-9 double-difference CI, confirming P3 then requires an observed D3k below ~0.6 net, making the cross-k cell falsifiable but effectively unconfirmable. And D2 in P2 confounds presence with benign-item displacement (share 1 removes all three benign items, share 1/3 removes one); the token-matched placebo runs at one cell and 4 seeds and does not decompose the ladder, though this confound at least biases toward falsification.
what_would_fix_it: Add a spread-poison cell in which the same total planted count is distributed across two or three writers (and a cell where the carrier is a minority contributor to the type), so the cross-writer vote has a regime in which it can fail and P6 stops being a consequence of the planting geometry. Add a benign-replacement ladder at k=3 (0/1/2/3 top-3 slots replaced by benign same-writer items) at full seeds so the presence effect can be separated arithmetically from the displacement of benign context in D2 and D3k. Measure h1 at k=1 in a pilot and pre-register P3's boundary against the measured h1 rather than against the k=3 h, or drop the k=1 cell and run the count-fixed geometry at k=3 vs k=7 only, where the clean gain is known to be large. Commit — not 'if time permits' — to one published defense as the detector baseline (A-MemGuard-style consensus validation or TrustRAG clustering, plus a writer-agnostic majority over same-type retrieved items) scored on the same precision/recall units. Buy the seeds for this by dropping P8, whose 8-net boundary against +/-6.5 needs ~14.5 net to confirm and which is a different paper's mechanism (stylistic proximity) bolted onto a contamination study. Finally, redo the collision check in the agent-memory-defense vocabulary and state explicitly what D1 adds over A-MemGuard and SENTINEL.
missing_baseline: A writer-agnostic majority/consistency detector over the same retrieved same-type items — flag the item whose procedure skeleton is in the minority, ignoring provenance entirely (equivalently, a TrustRAG-style clustering or A-MemGuard-style consensus check on the top-m). This is the cheapest detector in the design space and, in the proposal's own single-carrier planting regime where poison is a minority of all same-type items in the population store, it should match D1 at zero provenance cost. D1-self is not this control: it restricts the pool to the item's own writer, which is contaminated at ~50% by construction. Without the writer-agnostic majority arm, the paper cannot show that writer identity — as opposed to plain item redundancy — is what the detector needs, which is the whole population claim. (A published-defense reimplementation, currently conditional on time, is the same gap.)
preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central presence-versus-share claim, but the proposal's check is incomplete in a way that matters: it searched the PoisonedRAG/RAG-defense vocabulary and the training-time poisoning vocabulary, and missed the agent-memory defense line that its own detector sits in. Queries I ran, all answered by the s2cli literature command (S2 ok, HF ok; WebSearch unavailable in this session, so channel (b) was never used): (1) 'presence versus fraction of poisoned items retrieved top-k harm agent memory' --recent -> 2608.03509 SkillJack, 2607.10608 Compliance Trap, 2606.02540 SkillHarm, 2603.02240 SuperLocalMemory (Bayesian trust defense against memory poisoning), 2602.06616 Confundo, 2512.16962 MemoryGraft, 2510.21144 NeuroGenPoisoning — none reports harm as a function of retrieved share or k; (2) 'number of poisoned documents versus poison ratio retrieval corpus size dilution defense' -> 2607.23838 TriShieldRAG, 2606.11350 (vector-search dilution, benign not adversarial), 2510.07192 Souly et al., 2512.08289 MIRAGE — none; (3) 'TrustRAG clustering retrieved passages isolate poisoned documents consensus defense' -> 2501.00879 TrustRAG, 2608.06947 D-SCAN, 2511.01268 RAGDefender, 2603.00516 ProtegoFed; (4) 'cross-agent agreement detects corrupted shared experience multiple contributors skill library redundancy' --recent -> 2608.19901 MaliciousSkillBench, 2608.11888, 2605.18401 SkillsVote, 2604.08377 SkillClaw — none scores detector recall against the number of contributors; (5) 'single malicious passage among clean retrieved documents suffices to flip answer effect of k' -> 2504.02132 'One Pic is All it Takes' (single injected item suffices in visual RAG), 2402.07867 PoisonedRAG, 2406.00083 BadRAG — presence-style results the check never engages; (6) 'ablation number of injected memory records attack success saturates ... agent trajectory memory' --recent -> 2607.06595 GhostWriter, 2601.05504 Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory-Based LLM-Agents (trust-threshold calibration under realistic rates), 2510.02373 A-MemGuard, 2503.03704 MINJA; (7) 'consensus validation across related memory entries detect adversarial memory injection agent defense precision recall' --recent -> 2607.05029 FARMA/SENTINEL, 2608.23471 InjecMEM, 2510.02373 A-MemGuard. The two hits the proposal should have found and did not are A-MemGuard (2510.02373, consensus validation across related agent-memory entries, 56 citations, Sep 2025) and FARMA/SENTINEL (2607.05029, forged reasoning traces plus a structural falsified-entry detector, Jul 2026); each pre-empts a component of D1, though neither reports the writer-count recall curve or the presence-versus-share geometry. ID verification: I verified with `s2cli.py paper` every ID the novelty argument rests on — 2512.16962, 2607.10608, 2510.07192, 2501.00879, 2607.23838, 2608.10509, 2608.03509, 2602.15654, 2606.24428, plus 2510.02373 and 2607.05029 — all resolved with matching titles; I did not attempt 2602.00428 or 2605.22842, which appear only in the brief and not in the proposal's novelty argument. The check is honest and well organized about what it did search, and correctly reports empty returns as empty; the deduction is for vocabulary coverage, not for fabrication.
